question: A network architect considers a Cisco HyperFlex design solution for a company. The proposed solution is for a virtual environment that is not performance-sensitive, but the solution must have high storage capacity and a low cost. Which Cisco HyperFlex storage configuration should be used?
theory: HyperFlex Hybrid nodes pair an SSD caching tier with HDDs for the capacity tier, which yields high usable storage capacity at a lower cost per GB than flash-only designs, at the expense of the very low, consistent latency that All-Flash or All-NVMe configurations provide. For a virtual environment that is not performance-sensitive but needs high capacity and low cost, Hybrid is therefore the appropriate storage configuration, since All-Flash/All-NVMe are optimized for performance-sensitive, mission-critical workloads rather than cost efficiency, and 'All-SAN' is not a HyperFlex node type. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 15 — HyperFlex Storage Configurations, Hybrid Nodes)
